name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q01 - Volume conversion of cube into cubic metres

questiontext.text: A small cube has a side length of \( 1\text{ cm} \). What is the volume of this cube expressed in cubic metres (\( \text{m}^3 \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Side length of the cube: \( l = 1\text{ cm} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Unit Definitions
The relationship between centimetre and metre is: \[ 1\text{ cm} = 10^{-2}\text{ m} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
The volume \( V \) of a cube of side \( l \) is: \[ V = l^3 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the length in metres: \[ V = (1\text{ cm})^3 = (10^{-2}\text{ m})^3 = 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( (\text{m})^3 = \text{m}^3 \). The volume of the cube is \( 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q02 - Distance covered per second from vehicle speed

questiontext.text: A vehicle is travelling at a uniform speed of \( 18\text{ km h}^{-1} \). What distance does it cover in \( 1\text{ s} \)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Speed of vehicle: \( v = 18\text{ km h}^{-1} \).
Time elapsed: \( t = 1\text{ s} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Unit Conversions
Convert speed from kilometres per hour to metres per second using: \[ 1\text{ km h}^{-1} = \frac{1000\text{ m}}{3600\text{ s}} = \frac{5}{18}\text{ m s}^{-1} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Distance covered under uniform motion is given by: \[ d = v \times t \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Convert the speed: \[ v = 18 \times \frac{5}{18}\text{ m s}^{-1} = 5\text{ m s}^{-1} \] Calculate distance covered in \( 1\text{ s} \): \[ d = 5\text{ m s}^{-1} \times 1\text{ s} = 5\text{ m} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units check: \( \text{m s}^{-1} \times \text{s} = \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 5\text{ m} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q03 - Mass conversion from carat units into grams

questiontext.text: A gemstone has a measured mass of \( 15\text{ carats} \). What is the mass of this gemstone expressed in grams?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of gemstone: \( m = 15\text{ c} \) (carats).

Step 2: Assumptions and Unit Definitions
By standard unit definition retained for general use: \[ 1\text{ carat} = 200\text{ mg} = 0.200\text{ g} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Total mass in grams: \[ m(\text{g}) = m(\text{carats}) \times 0.200\text{ g/carat} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply the number of carats by the mass per carat: \[ m = 15 \times 0.200\text{ g} = 3.0\text{ g} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{carat} \times \frac{\text{g}}{\text{carat}} = \text{g} \). The mass of the gemstone is \( 3.0\text{ g} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q04 - Energy conversion between SI and CGS units

questiontext.text: Convert \( 1\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \) (which equals \( 1\text{ J} \)) into the corresponding CGS unit \( \text{g cm}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Quantity to convert: \( 1\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Base Unit Conversions
The conversion factors between SI and CGS base units are: \[ 1\text{ kg} = 10^3\text{ g} \] \[ 1\text{ m} = 10^2\text{ cm} \implies 1\text{ m}^2 = (10^2\text{ cm})^2 = 10^4\text{ cm}^2 \] \[ 1\text{ s} = 1\text{ s} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Substitute the converted base units into the expression: \[ 1\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} = (10^3\text{ g}) \times (10^4\text{ cm}^2) \times (1\text{ s}^{-2}) \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Combine the powers of 10: \[ 10^3 \times 10^4 = 10^{3+4} = 10^7 \] Hence: \[ 1\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} = 10^7\text{ g cm}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking dimensions: mass \( \times \) length\(^2 \times \) time\(^{-2}\). The converted value is \( 10^7\text{ g cm}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q05 - Volume conversion from litres to cubic metres

questiontext.text: A chemical container holds \( 4.5\text{ L} \) of solution. What is this volume in SI base units (\( \text{m}^3 \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Volume: \( V = 4.5\text{ L} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Unit Definitions
By standard definition of the litre: \[ 1\text{ L} = 1\text{ dm}^3 = (10^{-1}\text{ m})^3 = 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Volume in cubic metres: \[ V(\text{m}^3) = V(\text{L}) \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3\text{ L}^{-1} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given volume: \[ V = 4.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units check: \( \text{L} \times \frac{\text{m}^3}{\text{L}} = \text{m}^3 \). The volume is \( 4.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q06 - Total seconds calculation in one full day

questiontext.text: Calculate the total number of seconds contained in exactly one standard solar day (\( 1\text{ d} = 24\text{ h} \)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Time interval: \( t = 1\text{ day} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Unit Relationships
The conversion chain from day to seconds is: \[ 1\text{ day} = 24\text{ hours} \] \[ 1\text{ hour} = 60\text{ minutes} \] \[ 1\text{ minute} = 60\text{ seconds} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ t(\text{s}) = 1\text{ d} \times 24\frac{\text{h}}{\text{d}} \times 60\frac{\text{min}}{\text{h}} \times 60\frac{\text{s}}{\text{min}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply the conversion factors: \[ t = 24 \times 3600\text{ s} = 86400\text{ s} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: days cancel, hours cancel, minutes cancel, leaving seconds. Exactly \( 86400\text{ s} \) are in one day.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q07 - Plane angle calculation from arc and radius

questiontext.text: An arc of length \( \mathrm{d}s = 15\text{ cm} \) subtends a plane angle \( \mathrm{d}\theta \) at the centre of a circle of radius \( r = 50\text{ cm} \). What is the value of \( \mathrm{d}\theta \) in radians?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Arc length: \( \mathrm{d}s = 15\text{ cm} \).
Radius of circle: \( r = 50\text{ cm} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Definitions
Plane angle in radians is defined as the ratio of arc length to radius: \[ \mathrm{d}\theta = \frac{\mathrm{d}s}{r} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Ensure both lengths are expressed in the same units before dividing.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[ \mathrm{d}\theta = \frac{15\text{ cm}}{50\text{ cm}} = 0.30\text{ rad} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio is dimensionless, giving the unit radian (\( \text{rad} \)). The angle is \( 0.30\text{ rad} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q08 - Density calculation with significant figures retention

questiontext.text: A solid substance having a mass of \( 5.74\text{ g} \) occupies a volume of \( 1.2\text{ cm}^3 \). Calculate the density of the substance to the appropriate number of significant figures.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass: \( m = 5.74\text{ g} \) (3 significant figures).
Volume: \( V = 1.2\text{ cm}^3 \) (2 significant figures).

Step 2: Rules for Significant Figures in Division
In multiplication and division, the final result must retain as many significant figures as the input measurement with the least number of significant figures (here, 2 significant figures from volume).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Density: \[ \rho = \frac{m}{V} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Divide mass by volume: \[ \rho = \frac{5.74}{1.2}\text{ g cm}^{-3} = 4.78333\dots\text{ g cm}^{-3} \] Rounding to 2 significant figures (since the next digit is 8, raise 7 to 8): \[ \rho = 4.8\text{ g cm}^{-3} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The result retains 2 significant figures. The reported density is \( 4.8\text{ g cm}^{-3} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q09 - Sum of masses adhering to decimal precision

questiontext.text: Three separate masses are measured as \( 436.32\text{ g} \), \( 227.2\text{ g} \), and \( 0.301\text{ g} \). What is their total combined mass reported to the proper precision?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass 1: \( 436.32\text{ g} \) (2 decimal places).
Mass 2: \( 227.2\text{ g} \) (1 decimal place).
Mass 3: \( 0.301\text{ g} \) (3 decimal places).

Step 2: Addition Rule for Significant Figures
In addition or subtraction, the final result should retain as many decimal places as the input number with the least decimal places (here, 1 decimal place from \( 227.2\text{ g} \)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Total mass: \[ M = m_1 + m_2 + m_3 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Arithmetic sum: \[ M = 436.32 + 227.2 + 0.301 = 663.821\text{ g} \] Rounding to 1 decimal place (the digit after 8 is 2, so 8 is unchanged): \[ M = 663.8\text{ g} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The final value is properly rounded to 1 decimal place, giving \( 663.8\text{ g} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q10 - Calculation of one light year distance value

questiontext.text: If the speed of light in vacuum is taken as \( 3.00 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1} \) and one tropical year (\( 365.25\text{ d} \)) contains \( 3.1557 \times 10^7\text{ s} \), what is the value of one light year to the appropriate number of significant figures?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Speed of light: \( c = 3.00 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1} \) (3 significant figures).
Time in one year: \( t = 3.1557 \times 10^7\text{ s} \) (5 significant figures).

Step 2: Multiplication Rule for Significant Figures
The product must retain the same number of significant figures as the least precise factor, which is 3 significant figures.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Distance of one light year: \[ d = c \times t \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply the quantities: \[ d = (3.00 \times 10^8) \times (3.1557 \times 10^7)\text{ m} = 9.4671 \times 10^{15}\text{ m} \] Rounding to 3 significant figures (the fourth digit is 7, so 6 is increased to 7): \[ d = 9.47 \times 10^{15}\text{ m} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units check: \( \text{m s}^{-1} \times \text{s} = \text{m} \). The light year is \( 9.47 \times 10^{15}\text{ m} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q11 - Density of lead in SI units calculation

questiontext.text: The relative density of lead is \( 11.3 \). What is its density expressed in SI units (\( \text{kg m}^{-3} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Relative density of lead: \( \text{RD} = 11.3 \).

Step 2: Reference Standard Density
Relative density is the ratio of the density of the substance to the density of water at \( 4^\circ\text{C} \).
Density of water in SI units is: \[ \rho_{\text{water}} = 1.00 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \rho_{\text{substance}} = \text{RD} \times \rho_{\text{water}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[ \rho_{\text{lead}} = 11.3 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} = 1.13 \times 10^4\text{ kg m}^{-3} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{kg m}^{-3} \). The density of lead is \( 1.13 \times 10^4\text{ kg m}^{-3} \) (or \( 11300\text{ kg m}^{-3} \)).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q12 - Conversion of gravitational constant to CGS units

questiontext.text: The universal gravitational constant is \( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}\text{ N m}^2\text{ kg}^{-2} \). What is its numerical value in CGS units (\( \text{cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}\text{ N m}^2\text{ kg}^{-2} \).

Step 2: Base Unit Conversion
Since \( 1\text{ N} = 1\text{ kg m s}^{-2} \): \[ \text{SI unit} = \text{kg m s}^{-2} \cdot \text{m}^2 \cdot \text{kg}^{-2} = \text{m}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ kg}^{-1} \] Convert to CGS: \[ 1\text{ m} = 10^2\text{ cm} \implies 1\text{ m}^3 = 10^6\text{ cm}^3 \] \[ 1\text{ kg} = 10^3\text{ g} \implies 1\text{ kg}^{-1} = 10^{-3}\text{ g}^{-1} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ 1\text{ m}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ kg}^{-1} = 10^6 \times 10^{-3}\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} = 10^3\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply the SI numerical value by \( 10^3 \): \[ G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 10^3\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} = 6.67 \times 10^{-8}\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking dimensions: \( [\text{M}^{-1} \text{L}^3 \text{T}^{-2}] \). The value is \( 6.67 \times 10^{-8}\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q13 - Order of magnitude difference Earth and atom

questiontext.text: The diameter of the Earth is \( 1.28 \times 10^7\text{ m} \) and the diameter of a hydrogen atom is \( 1.06 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \). By how many orders of magnitude is the Earth larger than the hydrogen atom?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Diameter of the Earth: \( D_E = 1.28 \times 10^7\text{ m} \).
Diameter of the hydrogen atom: \( d_H = 1.06 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Order of Magnitude Convention
For a number \( a \times 10^b \): if \( a \le 5 \), the order of magnitude is \( b \); if \( 5 < a \le 10 \), the order of magnitude is \( b + 1 \).
Here \( 1.28 \le 5 \), so the order of magnitude for the Earth is \( 7 \).
For the hydrogen atom, \( 1.06 \le 5 \), so the order of magnitude is \( -10 \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Difference in orders of magnitude: \[ \Delta b = b_E - b_H \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ \Delta b = 7 - (-10) = 7 + 10 = 17 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The diameter of the Earth is 17 orders of magnitude larger than that of the hydrogen atom.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q14 - Estimation of hair thickness using microscope magnification

questiontext.text: A student observes the width of a human hair under a microscope of magnification \( 100 \). Over 20 observations, the average width seen in the field of view is \( 3.5\text{ mm} \). What is the estimated actual thickness of the hair?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Microscope magnification: \( M = 100 \).
Observed image width: \( w_{\text{obs}} = 3.5\text{ mm} \).

Step 2: Definition of Magnification
Linear magnification is defined as: \[ M = \frac{\text{Observed size}}{\text{Actual size}} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \text{Actual thickness } t = \frac{w_{\text{obs}}}{M} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Divide the observed width by the magnification: \[ t = \frac{3.5\text{ mm}}{100} = 0.035\text{ mm} = 3.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ mm} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
In metres, \( 0.035 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 3.5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m} \), which is physically plausible for human hair. The estimated thickness is \( 0.035\text{ mm} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q15 - Relative percentage error comparison of two masses

questiontext.text: Two mass measurements are taken with the same absolute error of \( \pm 0.01\text{ g} \). The first measurement is \( 1.02\text{ g} \) and the second is \( 9.89\text{ g} \). What are the relative percentage errors in the first and second measurements respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Measurement 1: \( m_1 = 1.02\text{ g} \), \( \Delta m = \pm 0.01\text{ g} \).
Measurement 2: \( m_2 = 9.89\text{ g} \), \( \Delta m = \pm 0.01\text{ g} \).

Step 2: Formula for Relative Percentage Error
\[ \text{Relative error} = \left(\frac{\Delta m}{m}\right) \times 100\% \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Compute the percentage error for each value independently.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \( 1.02\text{ g} \): \[ \frac{\pm 0.01}{1.02} \times 100\% = \pm 0.98\% \approx \pm 1\% \] For \( 9.89\text{ g} \): \[ \frac{\pm 0.01}{9.89} \times 100\% = \pm 0.101\% \approx \pm 0.1\% \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The relative errors are \( \pm 1\% \) and \( \pm 0.1\% \) respectively.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q16 - Total thrust force under standard atmospheric pressure

questiontext.text: What is the total thrust force exerted on a horizontal surface of area \( 2.0\text{ m}^2 \) by standard atmospheric pressure (\( 1\text{ atm} = 101325\text{ Pa} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Surface area: \( A = 2.0\text{ m}^2 \).
Pressure: \( P = 101325\text{ Pa} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Pressure is uniform over the flat surface, so force equals pressure multiplied by area.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ F = P \times A \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply the pressure by the area: \[ F = 101325\text{ N m}^{-2} \times 2.0\text{ m}^2 = 202650\text{ N} = 2.0265 \times 10^5\text{ N} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{Pa} \cdot \text{m}^2 = \text{N} \). The thrust force is \( 2.0265 \times 10^5\text{ N} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q17 - Discrepancy caused by intermediate premature rounding

questiontext.text: The reciprocal of \( 9.58 \) is calculated. If it is prematurely rounded to 3 significant figures as \( 0.104 \), its reciprocal becomes \( 9.62 \). If instead an extra digit is retained as \( 0.1044 \), the original value \( 9.58 \) is retrieved. What is the absolute discrepancy in the retrieved value caused by premature rounding?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Original value: \( x = 9.58 \).
Prematurely rounded reciprocal: \( y_1 = 0.104 \).
Retrieved value from \( y_1 \): \( x_1 = \frac{1}{0.104} \approx 9.615 \approx 9.62 \).
Correctly retrieved value: \( x_2 = 9.58 \).

Step 2: Relevant Principles
Rounding error in multi-step calculations causes deviation from the true original value.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Absolute discrepancy: \[ \Delta x = |x_1 - x_2| \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Subtract the original value from the prematurely rounded result: \[ \Delta x = 9.62 - 9.58 = 0.04 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The discrepancy between the two outcomes is \( 0.04 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q18 - Conversion of acceleration into kilometer hour units

questiontext.text: An acceleration of \( 3.0\text{ m s}^{-2} \) is expressed in \( \text{km h}^{-2} \). What is its value?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Acceleration: \( a = 3.0\text{ m s}^{-2} \).

Step 2: Conversion Factors
\[ 1\text{ m} = 10^{-3}\text{ km} \] \[ 1\text{ s} = \frac{1}{3600}\text{ h} \implies 1\text{ s}^{-2} = (3600)^2\text{ h}^{-2} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ a(\text{km h}^{-2}) = a(\text{m s}^{-2}) \times 10^{-3} \times (3600)^2 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \( (3600)^2 \): \[ (3600)^2 = 1.296 \times 10^7 \] Substitute: \[ a = 3.0 \times 10^{-3} \times (1.296 \times 10^7)\text{ km h}^{-2} = 3.0 \times 12960 = 38880\text{ km h}^{-2} \] Rounding to 2 significant figures: \[ a \approx 3.9 \times 10^4\text{ km h}^{-2} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{km h}^{-2} \). The value is \( 3.9 \times 10^4\text{ km h}^{-2} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q19 - Solid angle intercepted on a spherical surface

questiontext.text: A spherical surface intercepts an area of \( \mathrm{d}A = 0.072\text{ m}^2 \) at a distance of \( r = 0.60\text{ m} \) from the apex centre. What solid angle \( \mathrm{d}\Omega \) is subtended at the centre?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Intercepted area: \( \mathrm{d}A = 0.072\text{ m}^2 \).
Radius: \( r = 0.60\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Definition of Solid Angle
Solid angle \( \mathrm{d}\Omega \) is the ratio of intercepted spherical area to the square of radius: \[ \mathrm{d}\Omega = \frac{\mathrm{d}A}{r^2} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ r^2 = (0.60\text{ m})^2 = 0.36\text{ m}^2 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Divide the area by the squared radius: \[ \mathrm{d}\Omega = \frac{0.072\text{ m}^2}{0.36\text{ m}^2} = 0.20\text{ sr} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units check: \( \text{m}^2 / \text{m}^2 = \text{steradian} \) (\( \text{sr} \)). The solid angle is \( 0.20\text{ sr} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q20 - Conversion of one metre into light years

questiontext.text: Given that one light year is equal to \( 9.47 \times 10^{15}\text{ m} \), what is the value of \( 1\text{ m} \) expressed in light years?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\( 1\text{ ly} = 9.47 \times 10^{15}\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Conversion Principle
To find the number of light years in \( 1\text{ m} \), take the reciprocal of the light year in metres.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ 1\text{ m} = \frac{1}{9.47 \times 10^{15}}\text{ ly} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Divide 1 by \( 9.47 \): \[ \frac{1}{9.47} \approx 0.105597 \approx 1.056 \times 10^{-1} \] Combining with the power of 10: \[ 1\text{ m} = (1.056 \times 10^{-1}) \times 10^{-15}\text{ ly} \approx 1.06 \times 10^{-16}\text{ ly} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking magnitude: \( 1\text{ m} \) is an extremely tiny fraction of a light year (\( \approx 10^{-16}\text{ ly} \)). The value is \( 1.06 \times 10^{-16}\text{ ly} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q21 - Land area conversion into hectare unit value

questiontext.text: A rectangular plot of land has dimensions of \( 250\text{ m} \) by \( 400\text{ m} \). What is the area of this plot in hectares (\( \text{ha} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length: \( l = 400\text{ m} \).
Breadth: \( b = 250\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Definitions of Area and Hectare
Area in square metres: \[ A = l \times b \] By definition: \[ 1\text{ ha} = 10^4\text{ m}^2 \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ A(\text{ha}) = \frac{A(\text{m}^2)}{10^4\text{ m}^2/\text{ha}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate area in square metres: \[ A = 250\text{ m} \times 400\text{ m} = 100000\text{ m}^2 = 10^5\text{ m}^2 \] Convert to hectares: \[ A = \frac{10^5\text{ m}^2}{10^4\text{ m}^2/\text{ha}} = 10\text{ ha} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{m}^2 / (\text{m}^2/\text{ha}) = \text{ha} \). The plot area is \( 10\text{ ha} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q22 - Pressure conversion from bar into pascals

questiontext.text: The pressure inside an industrial autoclave is measured to be \( 3.5\text{ bar} \). What is this pressure expressed in pascals (\( \text{Pa} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Pressure: \( P = 3.5\text{ bar} \).

Step 2: Unit Definition
As given in the standard units table: \[ 1\text{ bar} = 0.1\text{ MPa} = 10^5\text{ Pa} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ P(\text{Pa}) = P(\text{bar}) \times 10^5\text{ Pa/bar} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the measured pressure: \[ P = 3.5 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{bar} \times \frac{\text{Pa}}{\text{bar}} = \text{Pa} \). The pressure is \( 3.5 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q23 - Subtraction precision with differing significant figures

questiontext.text: Two measured masses, \( 12.9\text{ g} \) (three significant figures) and \( 7.06\text{ g} \) (three significant figures), are subtracted. What is the proper value of their difference adhering to the rules of arithmetic operations?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass 1: \( 12.9\text{ g} \) (1 decimal place).
Mass 2: \( 7.06\text{ g} \) (2 decimal places).

Step 2: Subtraction Rule for Significant Figures
In subtraction, the result must retain as many decimal places as the number with the least decimal places (1 decimal place from \( 12.9\text{ g} \)), regardless of the total number of significant figures in the input values.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \Delta m = m_1 - m_2 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Subtract the values arithmetically: \[ \Delta m = 12.9\text{ g} - 7.06\text{ g} = 5.84\text{ g} \] Round to 1 decimal place (the digit 4 is less than 5, so 8 is unchanged): \[ \Delta m = 5.8\text{ g} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The correct reported difference is \( 5.8\text{ g} \) (which has 2 significant figures).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q24 - Total surface area and volume of measured cube

questiontext.text: Each side of a cube is measured to be \( 7.203\text{ m} \). What are the total surface area and the volume of the cube to appropriate significant figures?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Side length of the cube: \( a = 7.203\text{ m} \) (4 significant figures).

Step 2: Assumptions and Number of Significant Figures
In multiplication and exponentiation, the result must retain 4 significant figures, as the side length has 4 significant figures and 6 is an exact number.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Surface area: \[ S = 6 a^2 \] Volume: \[ V = a^3 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. Calculate surface area: \[ a^2 = (7.203)^2 = 51.883209\text{ m}^2 \] \[ S = 6 \times 51.883209 = 311.299254\text{ m}^2 \] Rounding to 4 significant figures: \[ S = 311.3\text{ m}^2 \] 2. Calculate volume: \[ V = (7.203)^3 = 373.714754\dots\text{ m}^3 \] Rounding to 4 significant figures: \[ V = 373.7\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The surface area is \( 311.3\text{ m}^2 \) and the volume is \( 373.7\text{ m}^3 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q25 - Uncertainty evaluation in rectangular sheet area calculation

questiontext.text: The length and breadth of a thin rectangular sheet are measured using a metre scale as \( 16.2 \pm 0.1\text{ cm} \) and \( 10.1 \pm 0.1\text{ cm} \). What is the area of the sheet quoted with its uncertainty?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length: \( l = 16.2 \pm 0.1\text{ cm} \).
Breadth: \( b = 10.1 \pm 0.1\text{ cm} \).

Step 2: Error Propagation Rules
When two quantities multiply, their relative fractional errors add: \[ \frac{\Delta A}{A} = \frac{\Delta l}{l} + \frac{\Delta b}{b} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Area: \( A = l \times b \).
Absolute uncertainty: \( \Delta A = A \times \left(\frac{\Delta A}{A}\right) \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Relative errors: \[ \frac{\Delta l}{l} = \frac{0.1}{16.2} \approx 0.00617 = 0.6\% \] \[ \frac{\Delta b}{b} = \frac{0.1}{10.1} \approx 0.00990 = 1.0\% \] Combined relative error: \[ \frac{\Delta A}{A} = 0.6\% + 1.0\% = 1.6\% \] Calculated area: \[ A = 16.2 \times 10.1 = 163.62\text{ cm}^2 \] Absolute error: \[ \Delta A = 163.62 \times 0.016 = 2.618\text{ cm}^2 \approx 3\text{ cm}^2 \] Rounding area to be consistent with uncertainty: \[ A = 164 \pm 3\text{ cm}^2 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The area quoted with proper uncertainty is \( 164 \pm 3\text{ cm}^2 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q26 - Total mass and difference of added gold pieces

questiontext.text: The mass of a box measured by a grocer balance is \( 2.30\text{ kg} \). Two gold pieces of masses \( 20.15\text{ g} \) and \( 20.17\text{ g} \) are added to the box. What are the total mass of the box and the difference in the masses of the pieces to correct significant figures?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of box: \( m_0 = 2.30\text{ kg} \) (known to 2 decimal places in kg).
Mass of gold piece 1: \( m_1 = 20.15\text{ g} = 0.02015\text{ kg} \).
Mass of gold piece 2: \( m_2 = 20.17\text{ g} = 0.02017\text{ kg} \).

Step 2: Decimal Place Consistency Principle
In addition, the result cannot have more decimal places than the least precise measurement (\( 2.30\text{ kg} \), having 2 decimal places). In subtraction of the two pieces, both are measured to 2 decimal places in grams.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Total mass: \( M = m_0 + m_1 + m_2 \).
Mass difference: \( \Delta m = m_2 - m_1 \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Total mass: \[ M = 2.30\text{ kg} + 0.02015\text{ kg} + 0.02017\text{ kg} = 2.34032\text{ kg} \] Rounding to 2 decimal places: \[ M = 2.34\text{ kg} \] Difference in mass of pieces: \[ \Delta m = 20.17\text{ g} - 20.15\text{ g} = 0.02\text{ g} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The total mass of the box is \( 2.34\text{ kg} \) and the difference in the masses is \( 0.02\text{ g} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q27 - Calorie value in arbitrary defined base units

questiontext.text: A calorie equals \( 4.2\text{ J} \) where \( 1\text{ J} = 1\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \). Suppose a new system of units is employed where the unit of mass is \( \alpha\text{ kg} \), the unit of length is \( \beta\text{ m} \), and the unit of time is \( \gamma\text{ s} \). What is the magnitude of one calorie in the new system of units?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Energy: \( E = 4.2\text{ J} = 4.2\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \).
SI base units: \( M_1 = 1\text{ kg} \), \( L_1 = 1\text{ m} \), \( T_1 = 1\text{ s} \), with numerical value \( n_1 = 4.2 \).
New base units: \( M_2 = \alpha\text{ kg} \), \( L_2 = \beta\text{ m} \), \( T_2 = \gamma\text{ s} \).

Step 2: Dimensional Formula of Energy
\[ [E] = [\text{M}^a \text{L}^b \text{T}^c] = [\text{M}^1 \text{L}^2 \text{T}^{-2}] \] where \( a = 1 \), \( b = 2 \), \( c = -2 \).

Step 3: Unit Conversion Formula
\[ n_2 = n_1 \left[\frac{M_1}{M_2}\right]^a \left[\frac{L_1}{L_2}\right]^b \left[\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right]^c \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[ n_2 = 4.2 \left[\frac{1\text{ kg}}{\alpha\text{ kg}}\right]^1 \left[\frac{1\text{ m}}{\beta\text{ m}}\right]^2 \left[\frac{1\text{ s}}{\gamma\text{ s}}\right]^{-2} \] \[ n_2 = 4.2 \left(\alpha^{-1}\right) \left(\beta^{-2}\right) \left(\gamma^2\right) = 4.2 \, \alpha^{-1} \beta^{-2} \gamma^2 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Dimensions check: mass power \( -1 \), length power \( -2 \), time power \( 2 \). The magnitude is \( 4.2 \, \alpha^{-1} \beta^{-2} \gamma^2 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q28 - Sun Earth distance in unit light speed

questiontext.text: A new unit of length is chosen such that the speed of light in vacuum is unity (\( c = 1 \)). What is the distance between the Sun and the Earth in terms of this new unit if light takes \( 8\text{ min} \) and \( 20\text{ s} \) to cover this distance?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Speed of light in the new unit: \( c = 1\text{ new unit s}^{-1} \).
Time of travel: \( t = 8\text{ min} + 20\text{ s} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Unit Conversion
Convert the total time into seconds: \[ t = (8 \times 60) + 20 = 480 + 20 = 500\text{ s} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \text{Distance } d = c \times t \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply speed by time: \[ d = 1\text{ new unit s}^{-1} \times 500\text{ s} = 500\text{ new units} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The distance between the Sun and the Earth is \( 500\text{ new units} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q29 - Linear magnification from projected slide area ratio

questiontext.text: The photograph of a house occupies an area of \( 1.75\text{ cm}^2 \) on a slide. The slide is projected onto a screen, and the area of the house on the screen is \( 1.55\text{ m}^2 \). What is the linear magnification of the projector-screen arrangement?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Object area on slide: \( A_1 = 1.75\text{ cm}^2 \).
Image area on screen: \( A_2 = 1.55\text{ m}^2 \).

Step 2: Relation Between Linear and Areal Magnification
Areal magnification is the ratio of image area to object area: \[ m_{\text{area}} = \frac{A_2}{A_1} \] Linear magnification \( m \) is the square root of areal magnification: \[ m = \sqrt{m_{\text{area}}} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Convert \( A_2 \) to \( \text{cm}^2 \): \[ 1\text{ m}^2 = 10^4\text{ cm}^2 \implies A_2 = 1.55 \times 10^4\text{ cm}^2 = 15500\text{ cm}^2 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Compute areal magnification: \[ m_{\text{area}} = \frac{15500\text{ cm}^2}{1.75\text{ cm}^2} \approx 8857.14 \] Take square root: \[ m = \sqrt{8857.14} \approx 94.11 \] Rounding to 3 significant figures: \[ m = 94.1 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: dimensionless ratio. The linear magnification is \( 94.1 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q30 - Surface area and volume of thin metal sheet

questiontext.text: The length, breadth, and thickness of a rectangular sheet of metal are \( 4.234\text{ m} \), \( 1.005\text{ m} \), and \( 2.01\text{ cm} \) respectively. What are the total surface area and volume of the sheet to the correct significant figures?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length: \( l = 4.234\text{ m} \) (4 significant figures).
Breadth: \( b = 1.005\text{ m} \) (4 significant figures).
Thickness: \( t = 2.01\text{ cm} = 0.0201\text{ m} \) (3 significant figures).

Step 2: Significant Figures Constraint
Because the thickness has 3 significant figures, the calculated total surface area and volume must be rounded to 3 significant figures.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Total surface area: \[ A = 2(l b + b t + t l) \] Volume: \[ V = l \times b \times t \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. Area calculation: \[ l b = 4.234 \times 1.005 = 4.25517\text{ m}^2 \] \[ b t = 1.005 \times 0.0201 = 0.0202005\text{ m}^2 \] \[ t l = 0.0201 \times 4.234 = 0.0851034\text{ m}^2 \] Sum of three face areas: \[ 4.25517 + 0.02020 + 0.08510 = 4.36047\text{ m}^2 \] Total area: \[ A = 2 \times 4.36047 = 8.72094\text{ m}^2 \approx 8.72\text{ m}^2 \] 2. Volume calculation: \[ V = 4.234 \times 1.005 \times 0.0201\text{ m}^3 = 0.0855289\dots\text{ m}^3 \] Rounding to 3 significant figures: \[ V = 0.0855\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The total surface area is \( 8.72\text{ m}^2 \) and the volume is \( 0.0855\text{ m}^3 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q31 - Atomic volume of one mole of hydrogen atoms

questiontext.text: The atomic radius of a hydrogen atom is approximately \( 0.5\text{ \AA} = 0.5 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \). Taking Avogadro number as \( N_{\text{A}} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1} \), what is the total atomic volume occupied by one mole of hydrogen atoms?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of single atom: \( r = 0.5 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \).
Avogadro constant: \( N_{\text{A}} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1} \).

Step 2: Assumptions of Spherical Model
Each hydrogen atom is assumed to be a sphere of radius \( r \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Volume of a single spherical atom: \[ V_{\text{atom}} = \frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 \] Total atomic volume of one mole: \[ V_{\text{total}} = N_{\text{A}} \times V_{\text{atom}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \( r^3 \): \[ r^3 = (0.5 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m})^3 = 0.125 \times 10^{-30}\text{ m}^3 \] Single atom volume: \[ V_{\text{atom}} = \frac{4}{3} \times 3.1416 \times 0.125 \times 10^{-30} \approx 5.236 \times 10^{-31}\text{ m}^3 \] Total volume for one mole: \[ V_{\text{total}} = (6.02 \times 10^{23}) \times (5.236 \times 10^{-31}\text{ m}^3) \approx 3.15 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{m}^3 \). The total atomic volume is approximately \( 3.15 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q32 - Molar to atomic volume ratio of hydrogen gas

questiontext.text: One mole of an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure occupies a molar volume of \( 22.4\text{ L} \). Taking the total atomic volume of one mole of hydrogen atoms as \( 3.15 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3 \), what is the ratio of the molar volume to the atomic volume?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Molar volume: \( V_m = 22.4\text{ L} \).
Total atomic volume: \( V_{\text{atomic}} = 3.15 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3 \).

Step 2: Unit Conversion
Convert litres to cubic metres: \[ V_m = 22.4\text{ L} = 22.4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Ratio: \[ R = \frac{V_m}{V_{\text{atomic}}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[ R = \frac{22.4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3}{3.15 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3} \] \[ R = \frac{22.4}{3.15} \times 10^4 \approx 7.11 \times 10^4 \approx 7.1 \times 10^4 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio is dimensionless and on the order of \( 10^4 \text{ to } 10^5 \), reflecting the vast intermolecular space in a gas. The ratio is approximately \( 7.1 \times 10^4 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q33 - Average mass density calculation for the Sun

questiontext.text: Given that the mass of the Sun is \( 2.0 \times 10^{30}\text{ kg} \) and its radius is \( 7.0 \times 10^8\text{ m} \), calculate the average mass density of the Sun.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of the Sun: \( M = 2.0 \times 10^{30}\text{ kg} \).
Radius of the Sun: \( R = 7.0 \times 10^8\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Spherical Geometry Model
The Sun is modelled as a sphere of radius \( R \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Volume: \[ V = \frac{4}{3} \pi R^3 \] Average density: \[ \rho = \frac{M}{V} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \( R^3 \): \[ R^3 = (7.0 \times 10^8\text{ m})^3 = 343 \times 10^{24}\text{ m}^3 \] Calculate volume: \[ V = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 343 \times 10^{24}\text{ m}^3 = \frac{4312}{3} \times 10^{24}\text{ m}^3 \approx 1.437 \times 10^{27}\text{ m}^3 \] Calculate density: \[ \rho = \frac{2.0 \times 10^{30}\text{ kg}}{1.437 \times 10^{27}\text{ m}^3} \approx 1.39 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \approx 1.4 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{kg m}^{-3} \). The density is approximately \( 1.4 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \).
